parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a national document/entry regime with this state's own hostile layer. Nationally, sex is redefined binary, X markers and self-selection are barred, passports showing birth sex are enforced at entry, and officers are told to refuse where doubt on sex arises and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility — a universal exposure with confiscation and stranding documented. Detention adds birth-sex custody with documented abuse in immigration custody. Locally, birth-certificate markers are closed (forcing disclosure), state-run facility use may be restricted, and the state lacks hate-crime or nondiscrimination coverage. Mitigants — national hate-crime law, pending litigation, 78% poll support, tribal gender traditions — are climate, not traveller protection.

entry_documents.exposure: National order bars marker self-selection and X markers; birth-sex markers enforced; Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where documents cast doubt on sex and weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility. Travellers report confiscation and stranding. The July 2026 assessment says this state's closed birth certificates force disclosure on document presentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, with limited waivers; litigation by a civil-liberties union pending; a legal-aid FAQ runs on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate into refusal → immigration detention → birth-sex custody; a foreign passport cannot be corrected here.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal); trans men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Custody counts no longer reported since 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document doubt under the Feb 2025 cable is the gateway from screening into this custody system for a visitor.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: April 2023 state law explicitly permits restricting trans people's bathroom use in many state-run facilities; nationally 21+ units restrict government-building facilities, 4 criminalise in certain circumstances, and one unit's trespass statute produced the March 2025 arrest (held 24 hours in a men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented criminal offence of this state's trespass type applying here; 29+ units have mapped bans; no presentation offence nationally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal building rules and state-run facility rules reinforce each other; private venues are less affected (bans in 6 units reach private settings).

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned in this state (April 2023) and nationally contested; proposed federal rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 hospital records in 2025.
care_services.protection: National employment/equality climate; emergency-care denial for trans visitors is not documented here.
care_services.interaction: A travelling parent whose minor is outed faces the state care ban plus federal order framing; adult visitor emergency care practice undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ memo uses 'radical gender ideology' among extremist-animating viewpoints; state party platform accused trans people of preying on women; executive orders frame care as mutilation and direct investigation of 'gender ideology' in schools.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward criterion excludes the phrase; counterterrorism powers stated not to target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined; a state party platform opposed by the governor and many delegates.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and lowers the odds police treat a trans complainant seriously.

minors_guardians.exposure: State May 2023 law requires disclosure of transgender students to parents in state-run schools; federal EO directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; state bans minor gender-affirming care and school sports participation.
minors_guardians.protection: National employment and hate-crime statutes, marriage equality; conversion therapy banned for licensed counsellors (June 2021).
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor carries marker-document exposure at entry plus care and disclosure rules if any state service is touched.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated violence incident against a trans person in this state appears in the sources; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity and 37 units lacked gender-identity bias statutes as of 2019.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; national crime data show sustained bias reporting rather than impunity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak state-level recourse pushes any identity-based assault onto federal prosecution, which is available but slower.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State has no gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime statute; religious-refusal service bill's fate unknown; birth-certificate rule relationship (2023 statute vs 2008 regulation) unresolved; facility-ban enforcement frequency unmeasured.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal challenges to passport policy and several 2025 orders are live; some orders blocked; 78% of residents backed an LGBTQ nondiscrimination law (2022); municipal protections in one city.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation is slow-moving and does not suspend measures left in force, so the traveller's operative rules remain the restrictive ones.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A this state permits facility exclusion by birth sex with weak remedy and no offence of being trans. It sits slightly above that anchor only because the mapped facility bans here reach government-owned rather than all public buildings and no court is recorded affirming the exclusion; it sits below on documents, where the national regime is harsher than 0.35-A's passport check.

Shared feature is a national universal-exposure practice with acknowledged-but-unremedied complaints. This case is worse than 0.45-D because the document regime can produce entry refusal and lifetime fraud findings plus confiscation/stranding, and because custody harm (immigration abuse, conversion-therapy policy) is documented, whereas 0.45-D's searches produce humiliation without custody consequences.

0.65-C rests on documented social acceptance, accepted foreign documents and functioning ordinary courts giving compensation. Here acceptance evidence is thinner (a 2022 poll and tribal traditions) while the traveller-facing document and facility exposures are concrete and operative, so this rates materially below that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: federal document and entry rules decide exposure, and the state adds a hostile layer rather than a shield. A trans visitor whose passport shows birth sex (the only option since 2025) carries a permanent mismatch risk at adjudication, hotel ID checks and any state facility; the cable's refusal-and-fraud language converts that mismatch into a possible detention pathway, and detention leads into documented birth-sex custody with abuse reports. Locally, closed birth certificates, permitted facility exclusion in state-run buildings, no state hate-crime or nondiscrimination law and a 'worst states' legislative ranking remove local remedy. Offsetting factors — national hate-crime coverage, pending litigation, public opinion support, tribal gender traditions — are real but climate-level and do not suspend operative rules.
